key_insight: Cova-PINN improves fluid-solid conjugate heat transfer prediction by enforcing conservation across thermal interaction paths, not just within separately sampled domains.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINNs more reliable for designing complex heat exchangers where accurate outlet temperature and end-to-end energy transfer matter as much as local field accuracy.
method: Cross-domain composite control-volume balances are enforced at the local scale.
Paired-wall closure is imposed at the exchanger scale to preserve global energy consistency.
Designed for complex multi-domain geometries such as TPMS heat exchangers and DualMS.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on four TPMS heat exchangers and one DualMS design, Cova-PINN reduced average outlet-temperature error by 37.7% and device-level closure error by 60.2% versus the closest baseline, MUSA-PINN-CHT.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurately defining conservation paths and wall pairings, which may be nontrivial in highly intricate geometries or incomplete mesh/geometry settings.
paper_title: Cova-PINN: Cross-Domain Conservation Physics-Informed Neural Network for Fluid-Solid Conjugate Heat Transfer in Complex Geometries
